title: Finite etale covers of closed subschemes of an affine normal scheme with separably closed function field (Stacks 09ZA)
statement: Let $X$ be an affine [def-pc-scheme] integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme] which is normal (every local ring $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is a normal domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]) and whose function field (the local ring at the generic point) is separably closed [def-pc-separably-closed]. Let $Z\subseteq X$ be a closed subscheme [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let $V\to Z$ be an etale morphism [def-weil-etale-morphism] with $V$ affine. Then $V$ is a finite disjoint union of open subschemes of $Z$: $V=V_1\amalg\dots\amalg V_n$ with each $V_i$ open and closed in $V$ and each restriction $V_i\to Z$ an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. If $V\to Z$ is surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism] and finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] etale, then $V\to Z$ has a section.

proof.text: *Affine description.* Write $X=\operatorname{Spec}R$ with $R=\mathcal O_X(X)$ [def-pc-scheme]. By part (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-affine-cover-criterion] applied to the closed immersion $Z\to X$ and the affine open $V=X$, the scheme $Z$ is affine and $R\to\mathcal O_Z(Z)$ is surjective; with $I$ its kernel, $Z\cong\operatorname{Spec}(R/I)$ over $X$, the morphism $Z\to X$ corresponding to $R\to R/I$ [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme]. Likewise $V=\operatorname{Spec}\overline C$ with $\overline C=\mathcal O_V(V)$, and the morphism $V\to Z$ of affine schemes is $\operatorname{Spec}$ of a ring map $R/I\to\overline C$ [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme]. Since $V\to Z$ is etale, $R/I\to\overline C$ is an etale ring map [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-map-iff-etale-affine].

proof.text: *Lift $V$ to $U$ etale over $X$ (Stacks: 'By Algebra, Lemma 04D1 we can lift $V$ to an affine scheme $U$ etale over $X$').* By [lem-exc-etale-algebra-lift] (Algebra 04D1: etale ring maps lift along surjections) there is an etale ring map $R\to C$ with $C/IC\cong\overline C$ as $R/I$-algebras. Put $U=\operatorname{Spec}C$; then $U\to X$ is etale [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-map-iff-etale-affine]. Moreover $U\times_XZ\cong\operatorname{Spec}(C\otimes_R R/I)$ [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] and $C\otimes_R R/I\cong C/IC\cong\overline C$ [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-quotient-base-change], all as $R/I$-algebras, so $U\times_XZ\cong V$ as schemes over $Z$.

proof.text: *Apply Lemma 09Z9 to $U\to X$.* The morphism $U\to X$ is a morphism between affine schemes, hence affine [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine], hence separated [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence] (part (3)); and it is etale (step 2). As $X$ is an integral normal scheme with separably closed function field, part (1) of [sbc-lem-etale-over-normal] gives nonempty, pairwise disjoint opens $U_i\subseteq U$ ($i\in\iota$) covering $U$ with every $U_i\to X$ an open immersion. The affine scheme $U=\operatorname{Spec}C$ is quasi-compact [lem-weil-pbc-spec-basic-opens-unit-ideal-quasi-compact] (part (iii)), so finitely many $U_i$ cover $U$; since each $U_i$ is nonempty and disjoint from all the others, no $U_i$ can be left out, so $\iota$ is finite, say $\iota=\{1,\dots,n\}$. Each $U_i$ is also closed in $U$, its complement being the union of the others.

source.place: Lemma 09ZA (label lemma-closed-of-affine-normal-scheme-with-alg-closed-function-field, line 14390), proof, second sentence ('Apply Lemma 09Z9 to U -> X'); Lemma 09Z9 (label lemma-normal-scheme-with-alg-closed-function-field), part (1)

proof.text: *Restrict to $Z$: the first statement.* Let $p:U\times_XZ\to U$ and $q:U\times_XZ\to Z$ be the projections and $V'_i=p^{-1}(U_i)$. These are open, pairwise disjoint and cover $U\times_XZ$ (step 3), hence each is also closed. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] (with base $S=X$, its open $X$, the opens $U_i\subseteq U$ and $Z\subseteq Z$) the canonical morphism $U_i\times_XZ\to U\times_XZ$ is an open immersion with image $V'_i$, compatibly with the projections; so $q|_{V'_i}$ is the projection $U_i\times_XZ\to Z$, which is the base change of the open immersion $U_i\to X$ along $Z\to X$ and hence an open immersion [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change]. Transporting along the isomorphism $V\cong U\times_XZ$ over $Z$ of step 2 gives $V=V_1\amalg\dots\amalg V_n$ with $V_i$ open and closed in $V$ and $V_i\to Z$ an open immersion: $V$ is a finite disjoint union of open subschemes of $Z$.

proof.text: *The section (Stacks: 'The final statement is a consequence of the first').* Assume $V\to Z$ is surjective and finite etale. The decomposition $V=\coprod_{i=1}^nV_i$ of step 4 into open and closed subschemes with $V_i\to Z$ open immersions is exactly the hypothesis of [lem-weil-pbc-clopen-open-cover-section] for the finite surjective morphism $V\to Z$, which gives a section $s:Z\to V$ (in that lemma the images $U_i\subseteq Z$ of the $V_i$ are open and closed, $Z$ is the disjoint union of the strata $\bigcap_{i\in A}U_i\cap\bigcap_{i\in B}U_i^c$ over $\{1,\dots,n\}=A\amalg B$ with $A\neq\emptyset$, and on each stratum the inverse of one open immersion $V_i\to U_i$ is used).
